newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares regress despite PLDT, inflation news.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares regress despite PLDT, inflation news.

text.p: * Main index down 10.52 pnts, or 0.32 pct, at 3,292.30 pnts
The Philippine stock market closed down for the second straight day despite the positive news of lower-than-expected inflation in February and PLDT's 100 percent stock dividend, brokers said.

"But the PLDT news along with strong buying on other commercial-industrial issues somehow pared down the losses which had taken the index down by 25 points," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asia Merit Securities Inc.
Traders said continued selling in index heavyweights San Miguel B and Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co prevented the index from sustaining its higher opening.
In the broader market, there were 60 advancers against 53 decliners. Trading volume was heavy at 19.358 billion shares worth 4.438 billion pesos.
Just before trading opened, the government announced that inflation in February had fallen to 4.4 percent from 5.0 percent in the previous month. The February figure was lower than expected.
"The market is still soft and we are still within consolidation on lack of any news," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
Jonas Ferrer, vice-president at Pryce Securities said, that Equitable Bank Corp's initial public offering which started today had begun siphoning some money from the market.
The focus could therefore return to less expensive second and thirdliner issues on Thursday, he said.
